messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — runtime eu-west-1: external exec/tool-call rate spiked to ~3.8x baseline; several pools hitting CPU/queue saturation. Auto-mitigation suggestions: tiered rate-limits, disable structured output (fn calls/JSON), fall back to text-only variants. Paging on-call.

sam: on it. starting triage — checking which tenants driving spike.

anya: initial query shows ~85% of spike from 6 tenants on free/standard plans, many calls contain tool/function signatures. Suggest targeted mitigation: 1) per-tenant exec rate cap (100 rpm) for free/standard 2) flip feature flag to disable allow_fn_calls for those tiers 3) force structured_output=false (text-only) for affected routes.

sam: agree. low-risk for prod tiers. ops, can we apply a scoped config change and confirm?

opsbot: running planned commands now.

```
# apply per-tenant throttle template (applies to free + standard)
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/services/configs/apply 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
  -d '{"scope":"tier:free,standard","changes": [{"path":"runtime.exec.rate_limit","value":"100rpm"},{"path":"features.allow_fn_calls","value":false},{"path":"runtime.output.structured","value":false}]}'
```

opsbot: changed config version v2026-03-17_01. Rolling to eu-west-1 pools (canary 3 nodes -> 50% -> all). Clearing local KV caches for routing.

michael: how many customers will see degraded experience? need to prep comms if any paid customers impacted.

sam: impact list: 6 high-volume free/standard tenants; no enterprise dedicated pools affected. Estimated customer-visible: tool-based automations will get text fallback or error for tool invocation.

jessica: i'll draft a short support note and a proactive email for the 6 tenants. Sam — can you attach a short cause + mitigations bullet list?

sam: sure: cause = sudden high fanout of external tool exec requests from ~3rd-party orchestration (spike pattern). Mitigation = tiered rate caps + disabled fn-calls + text-only fallback. Next steps = monitor 30m then consider gradual rollback when exec rate <1.2x baseline.

anya: observability update — 5m after change: exec queue length down 72%, CPU utilization in affected pools down to target band, 95th p99 token latency for streaming clients reduced ~40%. No new OOMs.

opsbot: enforcement logs: 6 tenants hit new rate caps, 2 tenants attempted fn call and received structured-disabled fallback (400 + message: "fn calls temporarily unavailable; falling back to text-only").

michael: thanks. I'll hold on the enterprise comms. Jessica, please send support note to those tenants; flag for account managers.

jessica: on it, drafting now. ping me for review.

sam: handing off monitoring to michael (next on-call) — watch exec rate and latency, and confirm no regression in downstream queues. If we see reaccumulation, escalate to infra.

michael: picked up. will watch dashboards and set alerts at 10m. tagging @pagerduty for on-call escalation window.

anya: adding runbook note: "if policy still saturated after 30m, increase per-tenant throttle to 70rpm and open temporary tenant quota hold; coordinate with PM for longer-term rate policy."

opsbot: rollback snapshot created (v2026-03-17_01 -> snapshot id s-1761239999).

sam: nice. next: schedule postmortem if we hold mitigation >2h. otherwise document incident in ops channel.

michael: will take ownership of post-incident writeup if mitigation persists.

jessica: support note sent to 6 tenants; added recommended mitigations for them (backoff, batching, reduce parallel tool invocations).

anya: metrics stable at 20m. leaving mitigation in place until traffic normalizes to <1.2x baseline for two consecutive 10m windows.

sam: thanks team — closing active page in 10m if stable. :white_check_mark:
